claims.title: Measured implementation activity
claims.statement: Top 0.029% by observed public GitHub push-event volume among 17.78 million active accounts, October 2025–June 2026. 35,896 GitHub contribution events across 318 active days in the profile manifest generated September 22, 2026.
claims.mechanism: A measured execution-frequency distinction supplies a real cohort rather than an invented prestige score.
claims.problem: A collaborator needs evidence that a large practice is more than a collection of plans.
claims.boundary: The fixed-window public push ranking includes automated accounts; it is not a Python-only, human-only, authored-commit or quality percentile.

claims.title: Protocol correctness accepted upstream
claims.statement: FastMCP accepted the OpenAPI object query serialization fix and regression tests in PR #3662.
claims.mechanism: Aligning formal interface semantics with actual request behavior.
claims.problem: Structured tool arguments must reach downstream APIs correctly.
claims.boundary: A bounded accepted fix, not ownership of FastMCP or proof of universal protocol expertise.

claims.title: Security tooling with fewer false positives
claims.statement: Datadog GuardDog accepted the git-URL normalization fix in PR #703.
claims.mechanism: Recognizing semantic equivalence instead of relying on brittle string comparison.
claims.problem: Security checks can misidentify equivalent dependency locations.
claims.boundary: The accepted change addresses this particular metadata mismatch, not a quantified security or time-saving outcome.

claims.title: Technical language as product behavior
claims.statement: Temporal accepted telemetry configuration documentation in PR #1385; dbt MCP accepted contextual OAuth wording in PR #669.
claims.mechanism: Making configuration defaults, interactions and authentication states intelligible to the user.
claims.problem: Working tools are still hard to adopt when their behavior is unclear.
claims.boundary: These are accepted documentation and interface-text improvements, not a measured adoption experiment.

claims.title: Instructions become validated interfaces
claims.statement: The maintained a-i--skills validator checks metadata, semantic fields, side-effect vocabulary, and additional core-tier requirements.
claims.mechanism: Treating instructions as structured, testable artifacts rather than disconnected prompts.
claims.problem: A collection of prompts needs consistent discovery, structure and declared behavior.
claims.boundary: Code inspection establishes these checks. Skill totals, inherited authorship, runtime support and efficacy are not inferred from this file.

claims.title: Organizational rules become executable constraints
claims.statement: Tool Interaction Design implements typed repository boundaries, registry/governance validation, policy-driven WIP limits, and offline-cache support.
claims.mechanism: Representing rules and lifecycle expectations in executable software.
claims.problem: Distributed work needs explicit policies and inspectable state, not implicit coordination.
claims.boundary: Implementation evidence is not fleet-wide operational success. No uptime or enterprise adoption claim is made.

claims.title: Humanistic concepts become computational objects
claims.statement: RE:GE contains a parser that turns symbolic organ and protocol commands into structured Invocation objects and invocation chains.
claims.mechanism: Designing a domain-specific language at the boundary between expressive intention and typed execution.
claims.problem: A creative or research domain needs tools that can represent its own concepts.
claims.boundary: This demonstrates an implemented formalization, not proof of research novelty, scientific validation or clinical efficacy.

claims.title: Cultural infrastructure with independent credits
claims.statement: Swamp Ape Review credits Anthony Padavano for its 2017 web design and as part of the 2018 marketing, events and social-media team.
claims.mechanism: Building the public interface and participation infrastructure around literary and hybrid creative work.
claims.problem: Creative work needs an accessible publication and audience-facing structure.
claims.boundary: Use the masthead roles as recorded. Do not substitute a sole-founder or editorial-chief title.

claims.title: An artistic record predating the AI-tooling work
claims.statement: ETCETER4 release pages date etcetera to May 1, 2012 and OGOD to March 1, 2015; the latter links an audiovisual counterpart.
claims.mechanism: Creating and releasing work in sound and image, not just building tools for other creators.
claims.problem: Creative technology benefits from a practice that has also made and released artifacts.
claims.boundary: Release-page dates and identity context are the evidence; popularity, sales, artistic superiority and uninterrupted professional tenure are not asserted.

pathways.title: Human intent into inspectable systems
pathways.thesis: Build across the gaps between what a person means, what a system encodes, what an agent does, and what a user understands.
pathways.problem: A tool-assisted workflow loses meaning between conversation, configuration, execution and handoff.
pathways.proof_product: One bounded workflow with source statements, structured requirements, acceptance tests and a replayable result.
pathways.outcome_measure: Measure task completion, incorrect handoffs, human correction time and unresolved ambiguity against a stated baseline.

pathways.title: Creative practice that can also build its instruments
pathways.thesis: Connect released artistic work, expressive domain models, and audience-facing publication infrastructure.
pathways.problem: The making, organizing and presenting of a creative body of work become disconnected.
pathways.proof_product: A credited artwork paired with a functioning tool that shows exactly how composition or interpretation informed its design.
pathways.outcome_measure: Document participant use, creative control, accessibility and repeat engagement; evaluate with an explicit artistic brief.

pathways.title: Systems people can understand and use
pathways.thesis: Combine executable structures with precise explanations and public-facing experiences.
pathways.problem: A system is technically available but its intended users do not understand what to do or why.
pathways.proof_product: A task-based onboarding sequence with a working example, a rubric and independently attempted completion.
pathways.outcome_measure: Compare unaided completion, time-to-first-success and recurring support questions before and after.

pathways.title: Research through making and testing representations
pathways.thesis: Turn an interpretive question into a domain model, an executable artifact and a testable investigation.
pathways.problem: A cross-disciplinary question needs both conceptual clarity and an instrument for investigating it.
pathways.proof_product: A bounded research question, artifact, comparison with prior art, evaluation protocol and public methods record.
pathways.outcome_measure: Report results and limitations against prespecified questions; distinguish creative contribution from validated research novelty.

discovery_lanes.title: Learning and capability transfer
discovery_lanes.question: Which instructional designs produced independently documented learning or task-completion gains?
discovery_lanes.required_proof: Dated course artifacts, anonymized outcome measures and attributable institutional or learner evidence; do not publish student records.

discovery_lanes.title: Artistic reception and production outcomes
discovery_lanes.question: Which released works have attributable credits, selections, audience response or client outcomes?
discovery_lanes.required_proof: Original credits, dated release pages, selection notices and aggregate analytics with reuse permission.

discovery_lanes.title: Measured client and institutional value
discovery_lanes.question: What changed because of the delivered work, rather than merely happening during the engagement?
discovery_lanes.required_proof: Named contribution, baseline, timeframe, result, attribution limits and permission to publish; protect commercial details.

discovery_lanes.title: Research originality
discovery_lanes.question: What proposition or method differs meaningfully from the closest prior art?
discovery_lanes.required_proof: Bounded question, literature comparison, artifact, evaluation and external review; implementation alone is not novelty.

discovery_lanes.title: External use of original systems
discovery_lanes.question: Who uses the work outside the owner ecosystem, and what do they accomplish with it?
discovery_lanes.required_proof: Independent use evidence, repeat use or maintenance signals, and scoped outcomes; stars and forks remain separate signals.

discovery_lanes.title: Further population-based distinctions
discovery_lanes.question: Which relevant comparative claims can actually be calculated using a matched metric, cohort and period?
discovery_lanes.required_proof: Replayable matched-population data and definition; no multiplied percentiles, synthetic genius score or repository-count proxy for quality.

publication_policy.pathways_are: Editorial problem-fit hypotheses, not proven scarcity, guaranteed demand or population rankings.
publication_policy.privacy: Only public approved sources enter the generated public atlas. Restricted evidence belongs outside this public repository; marking a committed secret private cannot protect it.
publication_policy.discovery: Follow source leads, then verify and add a dated record. This renderer does not fetch new evidence or run on a schedule.
publication_policy.authorship: Distinguish original design, maintained/adapted code, third-party components and agent-assisted implementation. Do not hide tools or erase the directing human contribution.
